findings.evidence: Opening paragraph 'Turn a Markdown document with embedded mermaid diagrams into a PDF (or a marp deck) in one non-destructive command...' restates the description and the Never list
findings.fix: Cut the intro to one line naming the script, or delete it; the description and the NEVER list already carry this

findings.evidence: 'Before you run, decide' gives three framing questions, but the Draft-or-final branch ends the same way either way ('any installed backend is fine' / 'let the quality-ranked auto-selection pick')
findings.fix: Swap the draft/final question for one that changes the action, for example 'Does the doc use LaTeX math or CJK text? Then prefer pandoc-latex or typst over chromium', so each question leads to a different command

findings.evidence: Environment facts such as '(SVG support on `weasyprint` is patchy)' and the --to html relative-link behaviour sit in table cells and prose, not in a Gotchas list
findings.fix: Add a short Gotchas list: weasyprint SVG is patchy; --to html keeps relative links and writes <stem>-assets/ that must travel with the HTML; mmdc needs a headless Chrome even when the mermaid source is valid

findings.evidence: The description has no 'Not for' boundary, though the trigger set has near-miss neighbours (DOCX/HTML to PDF, editing or merging PDFs, restyling an existing marp deck, one standalone mermaid diagram to PNG)
findings.fix: Convert a Markdown document (with embedded mermaid diagrams) into a PDF, or into a marp slide deck (pdf, pptx, html), in one non-destructive command; every ```mermaid block is rendered with mmdc and embedded. Use when the user wants to turn a .md file into a PDF or slide deck, 'export markdown to pdf', 'md to pdf', 'render mermaid and make a PDF', 'build a deck from this markdown', or asks which PDF backend is installed. Auto-detects the best installed backend (Pandoc+LaTeX > Typst > WeasyPrint > Chromium) and never auto-installs. Not for editing, merging, compressing or filling existing PDFs, for DOCX/HTML to PDF, for restyling an existing marp deck, or for rendering one standalone mermaid diagram. Keywords: markdown to pdf, md to pdf, mermaid, marp deck, slide deck, export pdf, pandoc, typst.

findings.evidence: examples/sample-with-mermaid.md is tracked, but SKILL.md, references/ and scripts/ never mention it
findings.fix: Reference it with a trigger (for example 'To smoke-test the installed toolchain, run the primary flow on examples/sample-with-mermaid.md') or delete it

findings.evidence: 'Hand the `.rendered.md` to `marp-slide` for themes/polish/export.' The handoff gives no instruction on keeping the sibling .rendered-assets/ folder with the file
findings.fix: Add: 'keep <source>.rendered-assets/ next to the .rendered.md; marp-slide resolves the diagram links relative to it'

findings.evidence: The script reports success as free text ('Wrote /path/source.pdf  (backend: <name>, diagrams: mmdc(<fmt>))'), and --help lists neither exit codes 2/3/4 nor any structured output option
findings.fix: Document the exit codes (0 ok, 2 mermaid or browser failure, 3 no backend, 4 backend failed) in the argparse epilog, and add a --json flag that prints {output, backend, diagram_format} to stdout

findings.evidence: Primary flow is 'Run, then report the printed result line verbatim'. No step checks the output, and nothing covers a document with no mermaid blocks or a missing local image
findings.fix: After exit 0, check that the output file exists and is non-empty, and state what happens to a document with zero mermaid blocks (plain conversion) and to a broken relative image link (which backend fails, which exit code)
